_comment: Ids from owed-baseline.txt that the CURRENT golden no longer owes (moved to SKIP/FAIL, or
dropped from cells.json) — named here with an owner and a rationale so the loss is a decision,
not silence. replay.sh reads this file; an id it does not cover is RED. `cells` is a regex over
the cell id (same convention as accepted-differences.json's `cells` field).
Coverage GROWING (a new id owed that was not in the baseline) needs no entry here — it is
always allowed and just printed; only a SHRINK needs to be named.
Nothing has been dropped from the 1.5.5 golden since owed-baseline.txt was generated from
Nothing has been dropped from the 1.5.5 golden since owed-baseline.txt was generated from
golden/1.5.5/ledger.tsv's PASS rows. The entries below are cells that have never been owed:
each is named here so the reason it is not recorded is written down and owned, and so the entry
is already in place the day the cell is baselined and then re-loses its fixture.

accepted.rationale: needs a tool-use verb in the pinned mock; product decision on the six-dialect tool-use response shape. The cell declared a mock_control the mock resolves to no verb, and an unresolvable control is served as a healthy 200 — so the cell would have recorded the tool-less happy path while claiming to pin usageMetadata.toolUsePromptTokenCount. The control is removed and the cell stays needs_fixture (SKIP) until the mock can answer with the tool-use token term and the product decides what that answer looks like in each of the six dialects; inventing either here would put the oracle's own guess into the golden.

THE REASON THIS ENTRY USED TO GIVE IS NOW FALSE, AND THE TRUE ONE IS OLDER AND LARGER. Until today this entry said the a2a plane had no recorder: record.sh refused the plane at its argument gate and again per cell, and `what an a2a cell needs is a DRIVER that speaks the plane ... and that driver does not exist on either side today`. Both halves have since shipped — v0.3.15 DELETED the by-plane skip and added plane-subject.sh, which drives the PRODUCT'S OWN conformance rig, and v0.3.16 made it ASK the rig what it can drive instead of reciting a table. Measured on the pin this tree carries, plane_scenario() answers with a real scenario for 13 of these cells, `undecodable-body` among them. So the tool is no longer what is missing, and an entry that goes on citing a closed reason is forgiving a gap for no reason. 
WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING, MEASURED 2026-09-11 ON AN IDLE ON-DEMAND FLEET BOX (i-08a313daa9fd90ab1, us-east-1d, load 4.00 on 32 vCPU, no proof on the box before or after): THE GOLDEN'S BINARY HAS NO A2A PLANE. The 1.5.5 golden is the PUBLISHED 1.5.5 binary (sha256 84bde0a0…), and the rig is a 1.6.0 rig. Driven through plane-subject.sh against that binary, h2_boot does not fail on a port, a fixture or a timing: the binary REFUSES THE CONFIGURATION, enumerating its own accepted top-level keys — `listen, public_url, tls, admin_listen, config, providers_file, admin_tls, admin_require_mtls, auth, identity-providers, providers, models, pools, hooks, groups, rate_card, per_request_fee, store, secrets, advanced, export, plugins, security, limits, health, routing` — and `agents` is not among them (`unknown field \u0060agents\u0060 ... at line 18 column 1`). The same binary's CLI surface carries no a2a, mcp or agent verb at all. The a2a plane is a 1.6.0 feature; 1.5.5 cannot be made to serve it by any fixture, any idle box or any tool release. 
SO WHAT IS OWED IS NOT A RECORDER RUN. A cell recorded from a binary that has no plane records nothing about the plane, and a BEFORE/AFTER pair whose BEFORE cannot exist is not a comparison — which is exactly what this entry previously promised (`recorded BEFORE and AFTER the change`). What would close these rows is a DECISION this register may not take for itself: either a second golden at a release that HAS the plane, against which 1.6.0 is the candidate, or the acceptance that the plane's first release has no predecessor to be diffed against and is proven by its conformance rig and its in-tree units alone. The change itself remains proven in-tree at crates/busbar/src/root/tests/units_a2a.rs, over both upstream shapes and over a lane-less leg. 
AND ONE HALF IS ALSO STILL BLOCKED ON THE RIG, INDEPENDENTLY OF ALL OF THAT. `no-agents-configured` is not among the 13 the tool can drive: ps_rig_can asks scripts/a2a-subject/h2-lib.sh's own h2_boot argument guard for a `lane-absent` configuration and the guard names only `probe|none`. `none` is the OTHER configuration that was wearing this row's name — it fronts nothing, so the submission is refused 401 in auth, upstream of the meter, and usage reads `requests: 0`, while this row's `why` states `{"requests": 1}`. The rig would have to grow the third configuration before the tool would drive it even against a binary that had the plane.

A GOLDEN DEFECT, named here so it is not leaned on — and the reason it is STILL a defect CHANGED on 2026-09-11, so the entry is rewritten rather than struck. The cell's committed file is byte-identical to billing|key-usage|after-1.json (both sha256 c4ed0dd0…ffa0): requests 1, spend_cents 250, under an id and a `why` that claim an upstream that was down. 
WHAT WAS WRONG, AND IS NOW FIXED. Its `pre` declares mock_control {"m-openai-chat": "down"} and no driver honoured a control written on a `pre` STEP, so the setup call ran against a HEALTHY upstream and primed the opposite state. oracle.pin v0.3.14 closed that: `run_pre_request` writes the step's own control before the step and clears it after, so the control cannot leak into the request the cell records. MEASURED on the pinned 1.5.5 (84bde0a0) at that pin: the pre now answers `pre POST /v1/chat/completions -> 503` where it answered 200 before, busbar_failovers_total{pool="m-openai-chat",reason="transient_upstream"} is 1, and the cell records `usage delta {}` — the refund it is named for — instead of the charged request in the committed file. The recorded bytes DIFFER from the golden-defect copy, exactly as intended. 
WHY IT IS STILL NOT RECORDED: THE CELL IS A COIN FLIP, AND A COIN FLIP MUST NOT BE FROZEN INTO A GOLDEN. Ten recordings — five on each of two different idle on-demand fleet boxes, same binary, same pin, same tree — produced exactly two distinct files in a 5/5 split. The whole difference is one entry of `applied`: `metrics.timing` fires on some runs and not on others. Everything else, `status`, `body`, and every member of `effects`, is byte-identical on all ten. The cause is in the recorder and is structural rather than flaky: `settle_then_snapshot()`'s quiescence probe digests the metrics exposition with `grep -v '_seconds'`, so `busbar_request_duration_seconds` — a SUMMARY, whose quantile estimates move with the clock and with the failover retry the down upstream now causes — is INVISIBLE to the settle loop, while `snapshot()` immediately afterwards captures it. Whether that summary moved between the two snapshots is therefore a race, and whether the delta has a timing sample to drop (which is all `metrics.timing` does; the effects come out the same either way) is a race with it. `applied` is the `norm.rules` diff class, so the flap is a real divergence the differ would report, not cosmetics. This never bit the cell before because the pre used to succeed and no failover observation landed near the snapshot boundary. 
WHAT IS OWED, AND BY WHOM. A TOOL release that either lets the settle probe see the metric families the snapshot records, or takes `applied` out of the recording's race with the clock. That is busbar-oracle's half, not this tree's: record.sh ships with the pinned tool. Until then the cell keeps its committed bytes, it is recorded and it PASSES, so nothing is owed by replay.sh; what is owed is a re-recording. No identity claim about a fee may cite this cell in the meantime, and none in this tree does — the refund is proven by the 45 requests-only rows of ledger.tsv.

THE TWELVE PLANE CELLS THE PINNED TOOL CAN NOW DRIVE, AND THE ONE THING THAT STOPS THEM BEING RECORDED. These are the a2a and mcp inventory cells on the transport and method each plane's conformance rig actually speaks — a2a's jsonrpc message/send at the fronted agent, mcp's streamable-http tools/call at the fronted server — crossed with the six outcomes the rig has a mechanism for. Asked of the pin this tree carries, plane_scenario() returns a real scenario for every one of the twelve, `mcp|...|tools/call|upstream_down` included: v0.3.16 probes scripts/mcp-subject/h2-lib.sh for the fault control that landed with h2-upstream-outage.sh rather than remembering that the mcp rig once had none. THE TOOL IS NOT THE GAP. 
MEASURED 2026-09-11 ON AN IDLE ON-DEMAND FLEET BOX (i-08a313daa9fd90ab1, us-east-1d, load 4.00 on 32 vCPU, no proof on the box before or after the run), driving all twelve through the pinned recorder against the binary the golden is OF: all twelve FAIL at the rig's boot, and not on anything a fixture could supply. The published 1.5.5 binary (sha256 84bde0a0…) REFUSES THE CONFIGURATION and enumerates its own accepted top-level keys — `listen, public_url, tls, admin_listen, config, providers_file, admin_tls, admin_require_mtls, auth, identity-providers, providers, models, pools, hooks, groups, rate_card, per_request_fee, store, secrets, advanced, export, plugins, security, limits, health, routing` — in which neither `mcp` (`unknown field \u0060mcp\u0060 ... at line 12 column 1`) nor `agents` (`... line 18 column 1`) appears, and whose CLI surface carries no mcp, a2a or agent verb at all. Both planes are 1.6.0 features. The rig is a 1.6.0 rig and the golden's binary is 1.5.5: there is no fixture, no idle box and no tool release that makes a 1.5.5 serve a plane it does not have. 
WHY THE ROWS ARE NOT LIFTED AND NOT LAUNDERED. A cell recorded from a binary with no plane would freeze the boot refusal of a config key under the name of a plane outcome, which is the same class of error as freezing a happy path under the name of a failure. They keep their golden SKIP rows and gain this entry, which names the one thing that would close them: a golden at a release that HAS the plane, or the owner's acceptance that a plane's first release has no predecessor to diff against. NOT IN SCOPE OF THIS ENTRY, and stated so it is not mistaken for settled: the 1,380 plane SKIP rows in the committed ledger still read `UNSUPPORTED: <plane> is proven by its conformance rig, not recorded here`, the by-plane excuse v0.3.15 deleted from the recorder. That text is stale and only a full re-record of the golden rewrites it; the reason above is the true one for all of them.
